subject: geography
title: Depositional Landforms & Periglacial
welcome_lead: Identify drumlins, moraines and periglacial features.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on glacial deposition, moraines, drumlins and periglacial processes.
final_note: Periglacial zones cover a quarter of Earth's land.

concepts.def: Unsorted, angular glacial debris deposited directly from ice.
Elongated egg-shaped hill of till; long axis parallel to ice flow.
Ridge of debris at maximum glacier extent; e.g. Cromer Ridge, Norfolk.
Sinuous ridge of fluvioglacial sand and gravel from subglacial stream.
Cold environment beyond ice margins; permafrost dominates.
Slow downslope flow of saturated regolith over frozen ground.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lodgement till is plastered beneath ice; ablation till accumulates on top during melting. Drumlins occur in swarms (drumlin field) like the Vale of Eden (>250 drumlins). Typical drumlin is 1-2 km long, 30-50 m high with steep stoss (upstream) side.

Terminal moraines mark glacier maximum (Cromer Ridge, Norfolk, 90 m high). Lateral moraines line valley sides. Medial moraines form where two glaciers merge. Ground moraine is the till plain left behind by retreating ice.

Permafrost covers about 25 percent of land in Northern Hemisphere. Patterned ground (stone polygons) forms from frost sorting. Pingos are ice-cored hills (up to 70 m) in Mackenzie Delta. Solifluction lobes form on slopes as little as 1 degree.

mcqs.q: What causes global sea level rise?
options: Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.

mcqs.q: What is a positive climate feedback loop?
options: Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
Positive feedback means a good outcome for the climate.
A process where warming triggers changes that cause more warming — e.g. melting Arctic ice exposes dark ocean, which absorbs more heat, melting more ice (ice-albedo feedback).
Positive feedback means the climate balances itself out.
